payload.description:
Harden the production command-worker image after the sandbox functional proof and before production deployment.

Scope:
- Use separate build and runtime stages while preserving lockfile-backed installation.
- Pin the Python runtime base by digest and document an explicit recurring update policy.
- Add a Dockerfile-specific .dockerignore and ensure the content address covers the complete copied runtime context.
- Exclude Poetry, compilers, Git, package-manager caches, VCS sources, and build residue from the final image.
- Preserve non-root execution with root-owned, non-writable application code.
- Configure writable runtime paths such as HOME, XDG_CACHE_HOME, and MPLCONFIGDIR beneath /tmp.
- Make the image compatible with a read-only root filesystem and narrowly scoped writable temporary storage where practical.
- Validate the declared linux/amd64 target and installed-package command-action smokes inside the final runtime stage.
- Record final compressed/uncompressed size and vulnerability scan findings before and after, with an explicit severity disposition.

Non-goals:
- Do not add ARM64 validation without a deployment requirement.
- Do not combine Lambda score-processor hardening into this task; its runtime constraints require separate work.
- Do not change command behavior or delay the current sandbox architecture proof.

Acceptance criteria:
- Final runtime contains no build toolchain or Poetry.
- The worker runs as its non-root UID with required caches writable and application code non-writable.
- The linux/amd64 image builds reproducibly and all enabled command-action container smokes pass.
- Read-only-root compatibility is synthesized or any unavoidable writable path is explicitly documented and scoped.
- Before/after size and scan evidence is recorded in Kanbus.
payload.title: Harden the command-worker container artifact
